quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from certain lanes. A green arrow means:

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
It means the same as a regular green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You can proceed only if the green arrow appears with a regular green light.
It shows the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same as a regular green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means the same as a regular green light. But drivers in that lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, you should:

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull over to the right side of the road and let other cars pass.
Not let the other cars pass you.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right side of the road and let other cars pass.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than the traffic around you can be dangerous. On a two-lane road, if traffic backs up behind you, you must pull over and let the other cars pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: When you see this black and yellow sign, it means:

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is roadwork ahead with a detour to the right.
Slow down because the road ahead makes a sharp turn.
There is a side road to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead makes a sharp turn.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead makes a sharp turn (in this case, to the right). Slow down before reaching a sharp curve the same way you would slow down for a turn at an intersection.

questions.question: You should use your horn when you:

options.text: Drive through an intersection.
Pass a bicyclist.
See a child about to run into the street.
Are parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: See a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: Fog makes it hard to see other cars, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Drive carefully and slow down.
Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road and objects better.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: In fog, it is hard to see other cars, pedestrians, and traffic signals. Drive carefully and reduce your speed. Do not use high beam headlights. Use low beams instead—they light up the road and objects ahead better in fog.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Stay farther back from the car ahead of you.
Drive carefully around all other vehicles.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: In snow, keep your windshield and mirrors clean. Increase the distance between your car and the car ahead because slippery roads make it harder to stop.

questions.question: Which driving technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Leave the highway as quickly as possible.
Use four-wheel drive.
Slow down and stay farther back from other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther back from other cars.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, the best ways to avoid crashes are to reduce your speed and increase the distance between your car and others.

questions.question: On a rural interstate highway, the maximum speed limit is usually:

options.text: 40 mph
55 mph
75 mph
85 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 75 mph
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit on a rural interstate highway is 75 miles per hour under good conditions. Always follow posted speed limit signs if they show a different limit.

questions.question: To be ready for anything ahead on the road, you should:

options.text: Look at the entire road and the sides of the road constantly.
Look straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal while driving.
Keep your eyes on the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and the sides of the road constantly.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead and watch for problems before you reach them. Do not just stare at the center of the road. Look at the entire road and the sides to see dangers early.

questions.question: Distracted drivers have a higher crash risk when using which of the following?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Cell phones (even hands-free ones) and audio devices like radios and CD players can distract you and increase crash risk.

questions.question: You are in an accident and your vehicle is blocking traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if possible. Do not leave the scene without telling others who you are and offering help.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.
Bumps in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You may not pass.
You may pass, even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means both directions can pass. You may only pass if it is safe and will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other vehicles?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Get in front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each pass increases the risk of a crash. If you drive faster than other cars, you will have to keep passing. Drive with traffic flow at the legal speed limit and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger directs you to stop.
When there is a stop sign.
When red lights are flashing and gates are down.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to, when there is a stop sign, or when red lights are flashing and gates are down.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand point upward. What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Come to a stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: Left arm and hand pointing upward means the driver plans to turn right. Adjust your driving if you are following a driver using this signal.

questions.question: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the car and walk for help.
Lay down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car because you will be found more easily there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car because you will be found more easily there.
questions.explanation: If stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you stay with your vehicle. Walking in a snowstorm can be dangerous.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you feel tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or passing on an interstate, signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spots. Only stop on the shoulder in emergencies. Change lanes as rarely as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, what should a small vehicle driver be ready for?

options.text: Loud noises.
Extra air pollution.
Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
Falling vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles. Small vehicle drivers should be prepared to steer correctly when passing large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
Work crew ahead.
Side road.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns of a sharp turn ahead and tells you to reduce your speed.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass. Make sure no cars are coming toward you.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot before passing.
When passing, wait until you see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When passing, signal at least 100 feet before you change lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Wait until both headlights of the passed car appear in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, driving from a curb, or merging is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not needed if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Checking your blind spot is important when changing lanes. Look over your shoulder toward the next lane. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: Before turning left, you should:

options.text: Use your horn.
Yield to oncoming vehicles.
Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic signal, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go first.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same way as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: At a flashing red signal, you must stop and let all other traffic go first.

questions.question: What can happen when alcohol is mixed with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both the alcohol and drug may become stronger.
Nothing will happen.
The effects of both the alcohol and drug may become weaker.
Only the alcohol's effects may become weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both the alcohol and drug may become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink taken with a cold medicine can affect you like you had several drinks.
